title: Sets Logic & Algebra I
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 200L Sets, Logic and Algebra curriculum: set theory and Venn diagrams, propositional/predicate logic and proof technique, relations and functions, binary operations, elementary group axioms, and mathematical induction.

questions.question: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5, 6}, what is A ∩ B?
questions.explanation: The intersection A ∩ B contains only the elements common to both sets, which are 3 and 4.

questions.question: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5, 6}, what is A ∪ B?
questions.explanation: The union A ∪ B contains every element that belongs to A, to B, or to both, without repetition.

questions.question: For a set A with n elements, how many elements does its power set P(A) have?
questions.explanation: The power set is the set of all subsets of A, and there are exactly 2^n subsets of a set with n elements.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly states one of De Morgan's laws for sets?
questions.explanation: De Morgan's law states the complement of a union equals the intersection of the complements.

questions.question: If A = {a, b} and B = {1, 2}, how many ordered pairs are in the Cartesian product A × B?
questions.explanation: The Cartesian product A × B has |A| × |B| = 2 × 2 = 4 ordered pairs.

questions.question: In a class of 50 students, 30 study Mathematics, 25 study Physics, and 15 study both. How many students study neither?
questions.explanation: By inclusion-exclusion, |M ∪ P| = 30 + 25 − 15 = 40, so students studying neither = 50 − 40 = 10.

questions.question: Two sets A and B are disjoint if and only if:
questions.explanation: Disjoint sets have no elements in common, meaning their intersection is the empty set.

questions.question: Which of the following is always true about the empty set ∅?
options: ∅ is a subset of every set
∅ is an element of every set
questions.correct_answer: ∅ is a subset of every set
questions.explanation: By vacuous truth, every element of ∅ (there are none) trivially satisfies membership in any set, so ∅ ⊆ A for any A.

questions.question: Which statement is a proposition in the sense used in propositional logic?
options: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria.
questions.correct_answer: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria.
questions.explanation: A proposition is a declarative sentence that is definitely true or false; questions, commands, and open sentences with a free variable are not propositions.

questions.question: The compound statement p ∧ q (p AND q) is true when:
options: Both p and q are true
At least one of p, q is true
Both p and q are false
Exactly one of p, q is true
questions.correct_answer: Both p and q are true
questions.explanation: Conjunction (∧) is true only when both component statements are true.

questions.question: The conditional statement p → q is false only when:
options: p is true and q is false
p is false and q is true
both p and q are false
both p and q are true
questions.correct_answer: p is true and q is false
questions.explanation: An implication p → q is false only in the single case where the hypothesis p holds but the conclusion q fails.

questions.question: What is the contrapositive of the statement "If it rains, then the ground is wet"?
options: If the ground is not wet, then it did not rain
If it does not rain, then the ground is not wet
If the ground is wet, then it rains
If it does not rain, then the ground is wet
questions.correct_answer: If the ground is not wet, then it did not rain
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of p → q is ¬q → ¬p, and it is logically equivalent to the original statement.

questions.question: A statement that is true under every possible truth assignment of its variables is called a:
questions.explanation: A tautology is a compound proposition that is always true regardless of the truth values of its components, e.g. p ∨ ¬p.

questions.question: A statement that is false under every possible truth assignment of its variables is called a:
questions.explanation: A contradiction, such as p ∧ ¬p, is always false no matter the truth values assigned.

questions.question: Which of the following is logically equivalent to p → q?
questions.explanation: The implication p → q is defined to be logically equivalent to ¬p ∨ q, verifiable via truth tables.

questions.question: In predicate logic, the statement ∀x P(x) means:
options: P(x) is true for every x in the domain
P(x) is true for at least one x
P(x) is false for every x
questions.correct_answer: P(x) is true for every x in the domain
questions.explanation: The universal quantifier ∀ ("for all") asserts that the predicate holds for every element of the domain of discourse.

questions.question: What is the negation of the statement ∀x, P(x)?
questions.explanation: Negating a universal statement yields an existential statement of the negated predicate: ¬(∀x P(x)) ≡ ∃x ¬P(x).

questions.question: A relation R on a set A is called reflexive if:
options: (a, a) ∈ R for every a ∈ A
(a, b), (b, c) ∈ R implies (a, c) ∈ R
questions.correct_answer: (a, a) ∈ R for every a ∈ A
questions.explanation: Reflexivity requires that every element of A is related to itself.

questions.question: A relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive is called a(n):
questions.explanation: By definition, a relation satisfying all three properties — reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity — is an equivalence relation.

questions.question: The equivalence classes formed by an equivalence relation on a set A:
options: Partition A into disjoint, non-empty subsets whose union is A
Always contain exactly one element each
Form a subset of A rather than covering all of A
questions.correct_answer: Partition A into disjoint, non-empty subsets whose union is A
questions.explanation: A fundamental theorem of equivalence relations states that the equivalence classes form a partition of the underlying set.

questions.question: A function f: A → B is called injective (one-to-one) if:
options: Every element of B has a preimage in A
f is both one-to-one and onto
A and B have the same number of elements
questions.explanation: Injectivity means distinct inputs always map to distinct outputs, i.e. no two elements of A share an image.

questions.question: A function f: A → B is called surjective (onto) if:
options: Every element of B is the image of at least one element of A
A is a subset of B
questions.correct_answer: Every element of B is the image of at least one element of A
questions.explanation: Surjectivity means the range of f equals the entire codomain B.

questions.question: A function that is both injective and surjective is called:
questions.explanation: A bijective function establishes a one-to-one correspondence between A and B, and is invertible.

questions.question: A binary operation * on a set S is said to be closed on S if:
options: a * b ∈ S for all a, b ∈ S
a * b = b * a for all a, b ∈ S
(a * b) * c = a * (b * c) for all a, b, c ∈ S
There exists e ∈ S with a * e = a
questions.correct_answer: a * b ∈ S for all a, b ∈ S
questions.explanation: Closure requires that combining any two elements of S under * always produces a result that is still in S.

questions.question: Subtraction on the set of natural numbers ℕ = {0, 1, 2, ...} is:
questions.explanation: Subtracting a larger natural number from a smaller one gives a negative result, which is not in ℕ, so closure fails.

questions.question: For the set of integers ℤ under addition, what is the identity element?
questions.explanation: Adding 0 to any integer leaves it unchanged, so 0 is the additive identity of ℤ.

questions.question: A set G together with a binary operation * is called a group if it satisfies which set of axioms?
options: Closure, associativity, identity element, and inverses for every element
Associativity and an identity element only, with no inverses required
questions.correct_answer: Closure, associativity, identity element, and inverses for every element
questions.explanation: The group axioms require closure under *, associativity, existence of an identity element, and existence of an inverse for every element.

questions.question: A group (G, *) is called abelian if, in addition to the group axioms, it also satisfies:
options: Commutativity: a * b = b * a for all a, b ∈ G
questions.correct_answer: Commutativity: a * b = b * a for all a, b ∈ G
questions.explanation: An abelian (commutative) group is a group in which the operation additionally satisfies the commutative law.

questions.question: Which of the following is a group under the operation of addition?
options: The set of even integers under multiplication
questions.explanation: The integers under addition satisfy closure, associativity, have identity 0, and every element n has inverse −n; ℕ under + lacks inverses, and ℤ under × lacks inverses for most elements.

questions.question: Using mathematical induction to prove a statement P(n) holds for all n ≥ 1, the base case establishes:
options: P(k) implies P(k+1) for arbitrary k
P(n) is true for all n
questions.explanation: The base step verifies the statement directly for the smallest case (usually n = 1) before the inductive step extends it.

questions.question: In the inductive step of a proof by mathematical induction, what must be shown?
options: That assuming P(k) is true, P(k+1) must also be true
That P(k) is true for one specific value of k only
That the statement holds for all negative integers
questions.correct_answer: That assuming P(k) is true, P(k+1) must also be true
questions.explanation: The inductive step assumes the inductive hypothesis P(k) and derives P(k+1) from it, which together with the base case proves P(n) for all n in the range.

questions.question: By mathematical induction, the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n equals:
questions.explanation: This is the classical formula for the sum of the first n positive integers, provable by induction on n.

questions.question: How many ways can 3 books be arranged in a row on a shelf (a permutation of 3 distinct items)?
questions.explanation: The number of arrangements of 3 distinct items is 3! = 3 × 2 × 1 = 6.
